body.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal S\) is absorbing, and write its distinct adoption dates as \(u_a=a(s_a)\).  Form the undirected graph \(\mathfrak G_{\mathcal S}\) with vertex set \(\{\bot,0,\ldots,p\}\) as follows.  For every \(a<b\) and \(t\in\{2,\ldots,T\}\), join \(t-u_a\) to \(t-u_b\) if both indices belong to \(\{0,\ldots,p\}\), and join the unique in-range index to \(\bot\) if exactly one belongs to \(\{0,\ldots,p\}\).  Then
\[
 \dim\ker G(\Pi)
 =\#\{\text{connected components of }\mathfrak G_{\mathcal S}\text{ not containing }\bot\}.
\]
Thus \(G(\Pi)\) has full rank for every positive law on \(\mathcal S\) if and only if every lag vertex \(0,\ldots,p\) is connected to \(\bot\).
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(v=(v_0,\ldots,v_p)^{\top}\in\mathbb R^d\), and extend it by \(\widetilde v_j=v_j\) for \(0\leq j\leq p\) and \(\widetilde v_j=0\) otherwise.  For \(a<b\), absorption gives
\[
 (E_{ab})_{t,j}
 =\mathbf 1\{u_a\leq t-j<u_b\}.
\]
Put \(x^{ab}=E_{ab}v\).  Since \(J\) is the orthogonal projector onto the vectors perpendicular to \(\mathbf 1_T\),
\[
 JE_{ab}v=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 x^{ab}_1=\cdots=x^{ab}_T
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 x^{ab}_t-x^{ab}_{t-1}=0\quad(2\leq t\leq T).
\]
The boundary convention and the displayed interval formula yield, term by term,
\[
 x^{ab}_t-x^{ab}_{t-1}
 =\sum_{j=0}^pv_j
 \left(\mathbf 1\{t-j=u_a\}-\mathbf 1\{t-j=u_b\}\right)
 =\widetilde v_{t-u_a}-\widetilde v_{t-u_b}.
\]
Hence \(JE_{ab}v=0\) for every pair exactly when the values attached to the two in-range vertices are equal for every graph edge and the value at every vertex joined to \(\bot\) is zero, where \(\bot\) carries the fixed value zero.  It follows that a solution is constant on each connected component, its constant is forced to zero on the component containing \(\bot\), and the constants on all other components are free and independent.  The solution space therefore has dimension equal to the number of components not containing \(\bot\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}support\text{-}rank}\), this solution space is \(\ker G(\Pi)\) for every positive \(\Pi\).  The full-rank criterion follows because the graph has precisely the \(d=p+1\) lag vertices in addition to \(\bot\).
body.justification: First differences turn the residual-kernel equations into equality constraints on a finite graph.
body.gap: A support-only matrix test does not itself reveal which ordered adoption endpoints identify each lag coordinate.
body.consumer: Applied code can return the disconnected lag components as a transparent rank-failure certificate.
